latency.method: Primary: pad probes on the v4l2src src pad and the v4l2sink sink pad stamp each buffer with CLOCK_MONOTONIC, keyed by buffer PTS (unchanged through queue/cudaupload/cudaconvert/cudadownload); added latency = sink-ready time - src-pad time, i.e. the delay our stages add over an app reading the camera directly (which receives the same buffer at the src-pad moment). Sink-ready = after the sink probe maps the buffer readable: cudadownload hands v4l2sink GstCudaMemory-backed buffers and CUDA work is asynchronous, so kernels and the device->host copy complete on first map; the probe's map does exactly the work v4l2sink's own map would do next. added_at_sink_pad_ms (before that map) is reported as a secondary figure and under-states the cost. Via consumer: a bench-only probe writes the PTS into the first 16 luma bytes just before v4l2sink; an in-process consumer pipeline (v4l2src on the loopback ! fakesink) decodes it on arrival on the same clock: camera src pad -> consumer receipt. Limits: excludes sensor exposure and USB transfer (identical for a direct reader, so it cancels); excludes the consumer app's own render/display (no glass-to-glass measurement); the stamp alters 16 luma pixels in bench mode only. gst_latency_query is what elements declare, not a measurement.
